citations.claim: N approach shows green at first violating step 127 while EW was green at 124-125 and yellow only at 126
E approach was in yellow at step 126 one second before forced switch to NS green

counterfactual.change: Removed the single emergency event at t=126 on N; otherwise identical, same 127 steps. This removes preemption so normal yellow plus all-red timing is kept and no violation occurs.

explanation: Emergency preemption at t=126 forces the emergency direction (NS) to green immediately: EW goes green at 124-125, yellow for only 1s at 126, then NS green at 127 with 0s all-red (need 4s) and yellow truncated to 1s (need 6s). The preemption path skips the yellow-duration and all-red clearance enforcement.

violation.detail: approach 0 turned green after only 0 s of all-red (need 4 s)

vision_note: EW approaches are green in steps 124-125 and turn yellow in step 126, then NS approaches are already green in step 127. There is no all-red clearance gap between the EW yellow and the opposing NS green.
